title: Global Express error handler returns err.message and err.stack to any client, pre-auth on any route

trace.description: POST /api/preview, any signed-up user (requireAuth); body.url passes the http(s) prefix check at line 11
axios.get(url) rejects on DNS failure, connection refusal, timeout or non-2xx status; the error carries Node's message (e.g. getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND <host>, connect ECONNREFUSED <ip>:<port>)
catch block forwards the raw error with next(err); no mapping to a generic message
res.status(500).json({ error: err.message, stack: err.stack }) for every error from every route; no NODE_ENV switch

evidence.description: Error handler serializes err.message and err.stack into the response body unconditionally
Comment states errors are returned on purpose so the frontend can show them; there is no production branch
express.json() runs before every router, so a malformed JSON body to any route (including unauthenticated /api/users/*) reaches the same handler: pre-auth trigger
Duplicate-email signup throws a SqliteError (UNIQUE constraint failed: users.email) that reaches the handler unauthenticated and discloses schema detail

counterevidence: Looked for anything that sanitizes errors before the response: no NODE_ENV check, no second error handler, no try/catch that rewrites messages, and preview.js:16 forwards the raw axios error. requireAuth (src/auth.js:22) gates /api/preview only, not the global handler; express.json parse errors and users.js errors are reachable without a token, as is a login with a known email and no password (scryptSync TypeError at src/auth.js:13). The handler sends only message and stack, not axios err.config or headers, so no request secrets leak. What can't be seen from the code: whether a reverse proxy or platform in front of staging/production rewrites 500 bodies. The ZAP alert in the input is an illustrative alert, not captured output, so it is not counted as reproduction.

likelihood.reason: Anonymous client can trigger it on any route with a malformed JSON body; no precondition beyond reaching the API

impact.reason: Discloses absolute install paths, module names, SQLite schema fragments, and (via /api/preview) whether internal hostnames resolve and their internal IP/port state; no credentials, tokens or user data

conditions.description: Assumes no reverse proxy or platform layer replaces 500 response bodies in the deployed environment; not visible in the repo
None for stack/path/schema disclosure (malformed JSON, signup errors); any signed-up user for the internal-network detail via /api/preview (open signup at src/routes/users.js:7)

title: semgrep tainted-sql-string on ORDER BY in GET /api/notes (sort is allow-listed)

trace.description: GET /api/notes reads req.query.sort (default 'newest') and uses it only as a key into SORT_COLUMNS
Missing key returns 400 before the query is built
Template literal interpolates order, the looked-up map value, not the request value

evidence.description: SORT_COLUMNS is a constant map of three fixed ORDER BY clauses
owner_id is bound as a ? parameter; only the map value is interpolated

counterevidence: Tried to get an attacker-chosen string into the template. Arrays and objects from Express 4's qs parser stringify to keys that aren't in the map (400), and a single-element array like sort[]=title only selects an allowed value. Inherited Object.prototype keys pass the truthiness check at line 14 but interpolate fixed text: constructor/toString/valueOf give 'function ...() { [native code] }' (SQLite syntax error), and __proto__ gives '[object Object]' (SQLite reads it as a bracket-quoted column name: no such column). Both are 500s with no attacker-shaped SQL and no data returned. qs 6.7.0 (package-lock.json) builds arrays/objects, not attacker text, for sort[] and sort[k]. The only way to make a lookup return attacker text would be prototype pollution elsewhere in the process; that is a separate candidate (the PATCH handler's _.merge at src/routes/notes.js:43, lodash 4.17.15) and not this claim. Sibling GET /api/notes/search at src/routes/notes.js:22 interpolates req.query.q directly and is NOT covered by this rejection.

ruled_out_by.control: SORT_COLUMNS allow-list lookup; the request value is used only as a key and an unknown key returns 400 before the query is built, so only fixed clause strings reach the template
